docs.title: App7 — language learning from reading (project write-up)
docs.text:
TL;DR

  • a Kotlin Multiplatform comic reader (Android + desktop) where every speech bubble is a lesson.
  • OCR-enriched pages, tap-to-annotate tokens, machine-translation zoom.
  • built solo in ~5 months, shipped behind a mechanical release gate.

docs.title: Why
docs.text: Reading is the most pleasant way to acquire a language, but comics don't come with a dictionary attached to the panel. App7 turns the comic page itself into the interface: you tap the word inside the bubble, and the help comes to you — in place, without leaving the story.

docs.title: The corpus
docs.text:
• 1.17M speech bubbles auto-detected across 6,724 chapters / 119k page images (14 series, 4 reading languages: de, fr, es, hi).
  • 226 chapters OCR-enriched into 127k word-level tokens, each with its bounding box and confidence (Tesseract / PaddleOCR / vision-LLM pipeline).
  • Machine translation with OPUS-MT: both a meaning translation and a literal one, with per-token source→target alignment — because learners need to know what the sentence means AND how it got there.

docs.title: The engineering
docs.text:
• Compiled domain ported Haskell → C → Rust behind a frozen 39-function C ABI: 58 Rust unit tests, a 100-assertion C round-trip parity oracle that passes unmodified (including a bit-exact xoshiro256** RNG), 25/25 Kotlin FFI parity tests, cross-built for 4 Android ABIs.
  • Cross-device sync on a 12-table Turso schema — and a war story: the first version did ~1.6M cloud reads for 32 writes. A one-round-trip max-rowid watermark probe cut steady-state reads ~360× (≈130k → ≈360 reads/hr), live-measured on device.
  • Ship discipline: a 16-feature × 3-target requirements-traceability matrix enforced by a fail-closed gate that greps marker strings out of the actual APK/AppImage binaries and superset-diffs against a pinned baseline — 110 logged automation runs over 14 Maestro e2e flows.

docs.title: The ML seam
docs.text: Token suggestions ship today as a confidence-ranked v0 behind an explicit interface (TokenSuggestionScorer). That seam is designed for my L1-aware vocabulary-difficulty model (2nd place, closed track, BEA shared task @ ACL 2026): the same architecture that predicts which words are hard for speakers of your first language will decide which token deserves your tap next.

docs.title: Hive Mind — a feed algorithm you own (project write-up)
docs.text:
TL;DR

  • a browser extension that uses your own recommendation model to filter major feed platforms.
  • trained on your annotations and those of a small circle of people you trust.
  • all served on your own compute.

docs.title: Why
docs.text: For anyone whose feed is decided by an engagement-optimized algorithm, the hive mind is a recommendation system you own: it filters your feed on the sites you already use, trained not by an ad market but by the judgments of a small trusted circle.

docs.title: The architecture
docs.text:
A thin layer injected into the browser gives two primitives — collect and annotate what you see. From there:

  1. In-page overlay on major feeds (LinkedIn, X, Reddit): mark a post good or bad without leaving the page.
  2. Per-group training pipeline in the cloud: each trusted circle gets its own ranker, trained only on that circle's annotations.
  3. Distribution back to the browser: the ranker is distilled to a small ONNX model that scores posts on-device — feed data never leaves the browser to be ranked. Private by construction.
  4. The loop: every correction you make is a training example for the next nightly retrain.

docs.title: The measurable outcomes (design targets)
docs.text:
The system is instrumented from day one for three numbers — these are the targets the build must hit, and the dashboard will show them publicly:

  • Capture: maximize good posts caught, under a hard bad-post leak threshold (a precision gate per circle).
  • Effort: minimize feed-triage minutes per member per week — the model should work so you scroll less.
  • Sharing: maximize the good knowledge that actually reaches the circle — what one member finds, all benefit from.

docs.title: Bernardo Stearns
docs.text:
Research Machine Learning Engineer & PhD Candidate (NLP)

Google Scholar · LinkedIn · Based in Ireland · Dual citizen: Luxembourg (EU) & Brazil

Profile

Research machine learning engineer implementing frontier NLP research models into industry partners. I design rigorous, reproducible experiments, pre-train and fine-tune language models at scale, and own the full path from research idea to deployed pipeline. My PhD and three EU Horizon 2020 research projects run on the same craft: adapting state-of-the-art models to hard, low-resource problems and engineering them into production with human-in-the-loop feedback.

docs.title: Insight Centre for Data Analytics — Galway, Ireland
docs.text:
Project Lead & Research Machine Learning Engineer · Jan 2024–Present

  • Leading the development of NLP pipelines to automatically generate and assess aviation exam questions from educational content.
  • Designed end-to-end workflows including model development, Dockerized deployment, and interactive dashboards.
  • Drafted project proposals and internal documentation (IDFs); project fully funded for extension due to client satisfaction.
  • Applied transformer-based models to assess question quality, ensuring reproducibility and scalability.

Senior Research Machine Learning Engineer · Jun 2019–Dec 2023

  • Core developer on two EU research projects: Cardamom — closing the resource gap for minority and under-resourced languages through deep-learning NLP and cross-lingual transfer — and Prêt-à-LLOD — increasing language-technology uptake by combining linked data with containerized, readily deployable NLP services.
  • Investigated how modern transformer models adapt to low-resource settings: built standardized, reproducible evaluation pipelines and benchmarked fine-tuning strategies (full, domain-adaptive, and parameter-efficient). Stack: PyTorch, HuggingFace Transformers, Weights & Biases.
  • Designed and built Teanga, a framework that composes containerized REST APIs into orchestrated NLP workflows — automated service-compatibility matching from OpenAPI specs, a visual workflow builder, and a CLI. Stack: Apache Airflow, Docker, OpenAPI, FastAPI.
  • Mentored MSc students and junior researchers in experimental design, model evaluation, and production-readiness practices.

Research Machine Learning Engineer · Dec 2017–Jun 2019

  • Built high-performance ML models for financial opinion extraction and text summarization.
  • Standardized reproducible experimentation pipelines; applied deep learning and NLP techniques (PyTorch, SpaCy, FastAI).
  • Contributed to multiple publications and research reports.
